To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the axons of single SNR cells form a local axon collateral network within the pars reticula and pars compacta of the substantia nigra and that the axons extend beyond the dendritic fields of parent neurons.
the axonal projection of single SNR cells forms an onion-like laminar pattern within the pars reticula and a longitudinal band within the pars compacta.

the local axonal projection of the GABAergic SNR neurons is organized in a laminar fashion, that the projection field of each neuron overlaps with that of neighboring neurons, and that the axonal projection of each SNR neuron is not confined within the dendritic field but extends beyond its limits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of the axonal projection fields of single neurons within the basal ganglia and the functional implications of this pattern.
the spatial organization of intranigral axonal projections of SNRs neurons.
the three-dimensional organization of a recurrent axon collateral network in a GABAergic nucleus of the basal forebrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the axonal network of the SNR neurons forms a three-dimensional structure that is organized according to the functional subdivisions of the SNR and the SNC.

the axonal projection of SNR neurons is not only involved in intranigral interactions, but is also involved in the control of dopaminergic nigrostriatal transmission through the indirect nigrostriato-nigral circuit.
SNR cells are involved in the processing of information in the basal ganglia, and that they participate in the regulation of the dopaminergic nigrostriatal pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SNR is an important integrative center for the basal ganglia circuitry.

, in the rat, SNR cells possess a complex three-dimensional axonal network that provides a substrate for the operation of both closed and open nigral circuits, thus enabling this nucleus to exert a powerful control of its own and neighboring basal ganglia nuclei.
the axonal projection of a single SNR cell can form a local inhibitory network in the SNR and a longitudinal excitatory band in the SNC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SNR is a complex nucleus that can be subdivided in a laminar fashion and that the SNR-SNC circuitry can be considered as an important part of the indirect nigrostriato-nigral loop.
the SNR neurons form an interconnected circuit with their dendrites, axons, and axon terminals forming complex three-dimensional patterns.
, in contrast to the striatum, the SNR is not a simple relay station but rather a complex processing center that is capable of integrating inputs and generating complex outputs.
